conflicts.quote: Session-bar aggregates are also In, as a third entitled class, because they are already paid for and they reconstruct the session’s price path at bar grain when a tick file is a miss or an empty extract.
conflicts.why: R1-architect lock 1 is stocks SIP trades_v1 + quotes_v1 only this slice. Mechanism already named: corpus identity is (et_date, product) with product enum {TradesV1, QuotesV1}; two universe-per-day stream GETs; reconstructable price/quote history is prints plus quotes. Aggregates are derived OHLCV — they do not add a tick the SIP trades file lacks — and they add a third vendor object, a third extract, and extra GB/day. BRIEF left this as a council lock; I am not claiming a new paid SKU (docs not in-repo list aggregates as already entitled). Shipping AC-3 as ship-blocking silently grows the product set and the store without that lock.
conflicts.proposal: Keep this slice to {TradesV1, QuotesV1} and leave a closed product slot. If the human locks session-bar aggregates In, extend the enum with a third independent class and a third universe GET; aggregates occupancy must never satisfy trades or quotes. Do not derive bars from the trades extract and call that the aggregates class.

conflicts.quote: Vendor day files are universe-per-day; the durable occupant is the locked-name extract per `(symbol, ET date, file class)`, not a promise to retain the entire US universe file forever.
conflicts.why: R1-architect lock 3 retains both the vendor gzip and the watchlist extract. Mechanism: stream GET to temp on the dedicated root → fsync → rename into a corpus locator; first-wins on successful corpus bytes (gzip magic + digest); extract may be rebuilt from that local corpus without network. After cancel, re-GET is impossible — that is the feature’s reason to exist. Extract-only makes a bad ticker-column filter or a later locked-name add a network operation, and leaves no entitled object to prove we fetched the universe file. Disk growth is an operator-volume problem; it is not a reason to drop the corpus object this slice.
conflicts.proposal: Durable operator-visible occupant stays the watchlist extract per (symbol, et_date, product). Also persist the universe gzip on the dedicated root as the first-wins corpus object (no prune this slice). If the human forbids universe retention, retract gzip keep and persist extracts plus a sidecar digest only; then extract rebuild requires S3.

conflicts.quote: Occupancy is miss or unreadable as appropriate — not kept.
conflicts.why: That outcome is paired with keep/fetch faults after due that include vendor down. Architect Miss is only due and vendor 404 / no-such-key after the due line. Transport or vendor-down without a 404 does not prove the object absent — that is Unattempted (UX download-failed: not confirmed). A truncated unusable body is Unreadable. Classifying unknown fetch failure as miss makes a later successful GET look like filling a hole that was never a hole, and collapses absent-is-not-none.
conflicts.proposal: Miss = due and no-such-key / 404. Unattempted = due and GET not run or transport/auth failed without absence confirmation (403/401 stay Unattempted/credential, not Miss). Unreadable = object/pointer exists but gzip/csv/header fails. Missing local S3 pair remains refuse-before-GET, distinct from all three.

conflicts.quote: Aggregates are derived OHLCV; they do not add a tick the SIP trades file lacks.
conflicts.why: The BRIEF left aggregates as a council lock, not Out. Session-bar aggregates are a third entitled class (S2, AC-3–5): bar-grain price history when a tick file is a miss or an empty extract. They do not add a tick, and they must not satisfy a trades or quotes claim — that is why they are a distinct class, not why they are Out. Skipping them is a scope/value call, not a tick-reconstruction fact. I will not silently narrow S2. The closed product `{TradesV1, QuotesV1}` and a two-product GET cannot represent AC-3.
conflicts.proposal: This slice keeps three independent classes: stocks SIP trades, stocks SIP quotes, and session-bar aggregates. Aggregates never classify trades or quotes as kept. If obtaining aggregates requires a new paid SKU, contradict AC-3 as feasibility; do not skip them as derived OHLCV.

conflicts.quote: Retain **both** corpus gzip and extract because a cancelled plan cannot re-GET (the feature’s reason to exist).
conflicts.why: The durable occupant the operator may claim is the locked-name extract, not the US universe file. Unbounded no-prune retention of GB-class universe gzip is a disk, volume-sharing, and license-adjacent cost, and it invites a “we kept the whole SIP day” completeness claim this slice forbids. Cancel-then-load of extracts (AC-10) does not require durable universe retention if the extract already succeeded.
conflicts.proposal: Operator claim and occupancy stay per (symbol, D, class) extract. Whether this slice also persists the entitled universe gzip (fetch artifact / post-cancel extract rebuild, no prune) is a human lock against GB-class volume growth. Either path must ban a full-universe keep claim and a completeness percent. I do not concede extract-only if rebuild-from-gzip is required; I do not silently accept unbounded universe retention.

conflicts.quote: Given D is due and the entitled class is not obtained, occupancy is **miss** — not not-elapsed, not empty extract, not an empty session-day tape, not not-storing.
conflicts.why: “Not obtained” after due collapses Architect Unattempted (GET not run, transport/auth failed), UX download-failed, unauthorized/missing-files-credentials, and vendor 404 into one miss. Architect Miss is due AND vendor 404/no-such-key. UX already forbids collapsing unknown fetch failure into miss. AC-15, the due-clock lock that says a class not obtained is miss, and the fetch-fault row that classifies faults as miss cannot stand under absent-is-not-none.
conflicts.proposal: Retract that breadth. Miss = due AND vendor 404/no-such-key after a keep. Unattempted / download-failed / unauthorized / missing-files-credentials stay distinct from miss, empty extract, not-elapsed, and not-storing. Fetch fault after due is not kept and is not automatically miss.

conflicts.quote: After the publish clock, a due absent vendor file is **`miss`**, not empty extract, not not-elapsed.
conflicts.why: On inspect (zero S3), “due absent vendor file” is store-absent, not a proved vendor 404. That is Architect Unattempted when GET was not run. Printing `flat files miss: vendor file for {ET_DATE} due and absent` fabricates a vendor hole and is the same collapse as AC-15.
conflicts.proposal: Miss literal only when due AND vendor 404/no-such-key is proved (keep path). Inspect of a due date with no stored object and no proved 404 uses a distinct unattempted/not-kept class, not miss. Empty extract and not-elapsed stay distinct. Keep CLI non-zero remains for proved miss.

conflicts.quote: Layout leaves a closed product slot so aggregates can be added later without restating provenance.
conflicts.why: PM locked session-bar aggregates In this slice as a third entitled class (S2 / AC-3 / AC-5), independently occupied and independently claimed. Parking them in a later slot is a silent Out: standing would name only trades and quotes, the list would omit the kind, and a bars-only keep could still be read as “the tape.” BRIEF left aggregates as a council lock, not an architect non-goal.
conflicts.proposal: This slice occupies three classes. Operator kind token is `aggregates` (never “session bars”, never “OHLC that proves open-to-close”, never a blended “tape”). Standing payload appends `· aggregates`. If the human takes architect Out, omit the column entirely — do not print `0 aggregates`.

conflicts.quote: Retain **both** corpus gzip and extract because a cancelled plan cannot re-GET (the feature’s reason to exist).
conflicts.why: PM’s durable occupant is the locked-name extract; full-universe retain is Future-dated. If the root holds the universe gzip, operator standing that says “not a full-universe keep” is a storage claim the data falsifies; if list/load serves that gzip, copy that says watchlist-extract-only is a redistribution/completeness lie. `kept` is an extract claim, not a universe-object claim.
conflicts.proposal: Operator-visible occupant and claims stay `(symbol, D, class)` extract. If gzip is retained as a fetch artifact, standing names it as a non-redistributed vendor object, never “we kept the whole SIP day.” Research load returns extract only — never the universe CSV.

conflicts.quote: Given D is due and the entitled class is not obtained, occupancy is **miss** — not not-elapsed, not empty extract, not an empty session-day tape, not not-storing.
conflicts.why: The operator literal I locked is `flat files miss: vendor file for {ET_DATE} due and absent`. That vouches absence. “Not obtained” also covers vendor-down, 403, truncation, and write-fail — none of which prove the file is absent. Printing `miss` there renames an unconfirmed fetch into a hole (`absent-is-not-none`). Empty extract stays the zero-row-on-a-present-file class; not-elapsed stays the clock class.
conflicts.proposal: `miss` only when due and vendor 404/no-such-key is confirmed, or inspect of a named due D with no stored object (BRIEF). Keep transport/unknown failure: `flat files download failed: vendor file for {ET_DATE} not confirmed` — not miss. Truncated stored body: `unreadable`. Credential failures never print as miss.

conflicts.quote: Auth 403/401 → `Unattempted` (credential), non-zero exit, no partial rename.
conflicts.why: `Unattempted` is not an operator occupancy word. It collapses GET-not-run, transport failure, and 403/401. A 403 after GET is a fetch, so it cannot stand in for missing-files-credentials or wrong-credential-class (zero fetch). Transport-without-404 is `download failed`, not miss, not empty extract. GET-not-run on a named due D with no object is inspect `miss` (BRIEF), not Unattempted.
conflicts.proposal: Type-level may keep a non-miss failed-GET state. Operator print: pair absent → missing-files-credentials (no GET); live key in the files slot → wrong-credential-class (no GET); unknown transport → `download failed`; confirmed 404 → `miss`. Never print `Unattempted`.

conflicts.quote: **Interface / PM** will not collapse occupancy into a boolean `present`/`missing` on the wire; the closed states (`NotElapsed` / `Miss` / `ExtractEmpty` / `Unreadable` / `NotStoring` / …) must remain distinct through to the operator consumer (`absent-is-not-none`).
conflicts.why: Distinctness must survive; the printed tokens must not. Operator success occupancy is `kept` / `kept from Massive flat files`, never `present`, never `Stored`. `Stored` is gzip-on-disk and would label a zero-row symbol as success. `ExtractEmpty` is not the operator string `empty extract`. Surfacing type names would rename the values.
conflicts.proposal: Map Stored + ≥1 extract rows → `kept from Massive flat files`; ExtractEmpty → `empty extract`; NotElapsed → `not-elapsed`; Miss → `miss`; Unreadable → `unreadable`; NotStoring → `not-storing`; Ineligible → `ineligible weekend`. Do not print `present`, `Stored`, `live`, `live_massive`, or `Live tape` on this vehicle.

conflicts.quote: Mechanism: new optional root; conflict predicate is bidirectional nest against ring, archive index, archive body, **and** the tape root; collision refuses process start (same as tape collision → `Err`, not disabled).
conflicts.why: A mis-set keep root would refuse `serve` bind. Traders would lose the desk. That is not `NO_UI_CHANGE` and not live-tick isolation. PM’s collision outcome is keep **refuse to mix** with tape/archive/ring unchanged; not-storing is unset/unwritable, a different class. Architect’s own armed-keep rule says collision refuse is on the armed construct, not on `serve`.
conflicts.proposal: Collision refuses armed keep (`refuse to mix`) and occupies none of those roots. `serve` still binds and talks to Massive REST/WS. Operator line is not `flat files not storing`.

conflicts.quote: Mechanism: files client type **has no `api_key` field**; it takes an access-key + secret pair loaded from env **other than** `MASSIVE_API_KEY`.
conflicts.why: Different env names do not detect the live REST/WS key placed in the files slot. SigV4 would still GET and 403 as `Unattempted` — a fetch, and not PM’s wrong-credential-class refuse with files-call count 0. Operator copy cannot say “does not fetch” or distinguish that refuse from missing pair or from miss.
conflicts.proposal: Armed keep classifies the files pair against the live REST key before any GET. Equal/wrong class → refuse, zero files fetch, literal wrong-credential-class. Missing pair → missing-files-credentials, zero fetch. Source scan on the files leaf remains.

conflicts.quote: Not-elapsed, miss, empty extract, unreadable, not-storing, missing-files-credentials, wrong-credential-class, ineligible-weekend, not-in-watchlist, unauthorized, kept, live-tape, and live-paid-present outcomes are distinguishable in operator keep/list/load without reading source.
conflicts.why: Listing `live-tape` and `live-paid-present` as keep/list/load outcomes puts poison tokens on this vehicle. Success occupancy is `kept`, never `present`. `live tape` is a foreign class (session-day-tape / ticker Live tape) and must not appear as a flat-file cell. The same AC then bans coverage/tape literals as this occupancy — the outcome list contradicts the ban and the `live` / `live_massive` / `present` poison.
conflicts.proposal: This vehicle’s printed deck is kept · not-elapsed · miss · empty extract · unreadable · not-storing · missing-files-credentials · wrong-credential-class · ineligible-weekend · not-in-watchlist · unauthorized (HTTP). live-tape and live-paid-present are distinguished by absence; poison tests fail if those literals appear here.

conflicts.quote: Armed keep with missing/unusable S3 keys yields **`flat files unauthorized`** and the clause **REST apiKey is not the S3 secret**.
conflicts.why: I collapsed three classes into one line. PM requires missing-files-credentials ≠ wrong-credential-class ≠ HTTP unauthorized. Printing the REST-apiKey clause on a mere missing pair asserts a substitution this run did not perform — copy that the data does not support.
conflicts.proposal: Missing pair → `flat files unauthorized` (or missing-files-credentials) with no REST clause and no fetch. Live key in the files slot → wrong-credential-class + `REST apiKey is not the files secret` + no fetch. HTTP token miss → shipped `metrics_unauthorized` only.

conflicts.quote: Extract:     watchlist rows only · not a full-universe keep · not a full open-to-close claim
conflicts.why: “Not a full-universe keep” is a storage fact I cannot vouch until the occupant lock lands. If architect retains the universe gzip, that standing line is false. The still-defensible hedges are no redistribution and no open-to-close completeness claim from a filtered extract.
conflicts.proposal: Standing: product occupant is the watchlist extract · not a full-universe redistribution · not a full open-to-close claim. Drop “not a full-universe keep” as a store assertion.
